NKE.rationale: Nike is exhibiting severe, multi-quarter fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term stabilization. Q3 FY26 diluted EPS fell 35.2% YoY to $0.35, operating cash flow collapsed 76% to $430M, and net margin has halved to 4.8% from 9.4% a year ago. Revenue is flat at $11.28B with management guiding Q4 to decline 2-4% and recovery pushed to Q2 FY2027. Two strategic pillars — Greater China (down 16% with 850bps margin collapse) and Converse (down 35%) — are in structural decline without clear recovery timelines. At 29x trailing PE, the market is paying a higher multiple for a business generating half the profitability of a year ago, while ROE has collapsed from 32.2% to 16.0%. The macro backdrop compounds the headwinds: oil at $100.2/bbl, 10-year yield at 4.57%, and tariffs adding ~$1B in costs. Competitive share is eroding to On, Hoka, and New Balance. The only bright spots — running category up 20%+ and North America wholesale growth — are insufficient to offset the China/Converse/tariff overhangs. No near-term catalyst exists to re-rate the stock; the turnaround lacks visible traction in its most troubled segments.
